craft_claim: A reverent passage is aimed at an object the speaker experiences as beyond full grasp; if the narrator has fully captured, explained, or priced the object, the register is borrowed rather than reverent.

supporting_evidence.location: The Idea of the Holy, chs. II-VI
supporting_evidence.note: Otto names the numinous as a non-rational, non-sensory state whose object is ganz Andere ('wholly other'), analysed as mysterium tremendum et fascinans - daunting and compelling at once - and as sui generis.

supporting_evidence.location: Four Quartets, recurrence of the 'still point' and imagery of fire and rose
supporting_evidence.note: Eliot's meditation repeatedly circles a reality it cannot state directly, letting figures approach what the poem declines to define.

scope: Recognition criterion for distinguishing genuine sacred attention from performed solemnity; applies across devotional and secular-profound prose.
exceptions: Teaching or exegetical passages may name and analyse the sacred without dissolving it, provided the analysis acknowledges its own limits.
